content:
Elliot Price: We keep using “agent” in a few places in the quickstart READMEs + docs pages. I’m worried it reads like “Redwood Agents” (internal feature) vs “app that calls tools in a loop.” Can we align terminology before PR-842/843 merge?

Wei Chen: +1. In the walkthrough I wrote “Agent Quickstart” and then later “Workflow” and “Orchestrator” interchangeably. It’s muddy.

Monica Patel: yep, we’ve had confusion already in review. internal folks assume it’s the “Agents” product workstream.

Henry Cho: from PM side: we should avoid implying a product surface we don’t ship. Also avoid “agents” as a Redwood feature name.

Elliot Price: Proposal: in docs nav and H1s we call it “RAG + tool-calling workflow” or “RAG + tool-calling loop” and then define “agent loop” once.

Renee Sullivan: external devs search for “agent” though. If we avoid the word entirely, we might hurt discoverability.

Nikhil Sharma: agree w/ Renee. Also our internal telemetry/event naming uses `template_type=rag_agent` right now. Not user-facing, but it’s in code comments.

Wei Chen: maybe: “Agentic workflow (tool calling)”? But “agentic” feels jargon-y.

Monica Patel: another angle: keep “agent” but always qualify as “tool-calling agent loop” and add a callout: “This is not the Redwood Agents product.”

Elliot Price: I like that. We can do a short “Terminology” section near the top of each template README.

Allison Grant: +1 please add the note. Also in observability docs, span names include `agent.step` today. If we rename, we should decide now.

Wei Chen: Can we settle on a consistent set:
- RAG = retrieval-augmented generation (retriever + context injection)
- tool = external function/API the model calls
- agent loop = repeated: model -> tool -> model, with max iterations
- workflow = the overall app pipeline (RAG, tool calls, post-processing)

Henry Cho: works. Strong preference: “workflow” as the umbrella term.

Renee Sullivan: What about the landing page / nav label? “RAG + Agents” is super clear to devs.

Elliot Price: nav label is the hardest part. If we put “RAG + Agents” in nav, we’ll get internal confusion; if we remove “Agents,” we lose external clarity.

Monica Patel: maybe nav: “RAG + Tool Calling (Agents)”? Parenthetical keeps search + sets expectation.

Nikhil Sharma: +1. Also mirrors what a lot of OSS projects do.

Wei Chen: For the doc copy, we can do:
“RAG + Tool Calling (Agents)
Build a retrieval-augmented app with a simple tool-calling agent loop. (Not related to any Redwood product feature named ‘Agents’.)”

Elliot Price: that’s good. Also in the README, replace “Agent service” with “Orchestrator service” or “App server”? “Agent service” sounds like a product.

Monica Patel: +1 rename in repo:
- `agent.py` / `agent.ts` is fine (code)
- but README headings should say “Tool-calling loop” / “Orchestrator”

Allison Grant: On spans: current:
- `rag.retrieve`
- `agent.step`
- `tool.call`
I’d rather keep `agent.step` (it matches what people expect), but we can document “agent step = one LLM decision turn.” Also avoid adding “workflow.*” spans, it’s too vague.

Wei Chen: ok, and in docs I’ll add a glossary + “not Redwood Agents product” note.

Henry Cho: can we avoid the phrase “Redwood Agents” entirely in public docs? That’s internal-only.

Elliot Price: good point. The note should be generic: “This template demonstrates an agent loop pattern (tool calling). It is not a separate Redwood product feature.”

Renee Sullivan: +1 keep it generic.

Monica Patel: what about filenames in docs repo? There’s `rag-agent-template-walkthrough.mdx` in PR-842.

Elliot Price: Let’s keep filename for now (not user visible), but page title/H1 becomes “RAG + Tool Calling (Agents) Quickstart” and slug can stay.

Nikhil Sharma: also in examples we use “agent” in code comments. I’ll sweep for “Agents product” phrasing and remove.

Wei Chen: I’ll update:
- docs page intro + glossary
- README “Terminology” + “What this template is / isn’t” section
- replace “agent framework” wording w/ “tool-calling loop”

Allison Grant: pls ping me on the wording so I can mirror in observability hooks reference. Also ensure the dashboard names don’t say “Agents product.”

Elliot Price: Action items:
1) Wei: add glossary + callout + update headings (PR-842 follow-up)
2) Monica: quick pass on template READMEs for wording + heading consistency
3) Elliot: update docs IA/nav label to “RAG + Tool Calling (Agents)” and add a short tooltip sentence

Renee Sullivan: :thumbsup: once it lands I’ll also adjust the launch brief messaging so we don’t say “Redwood Agents.”

Henry Cho: +1. Thanks all.

Wei Chen: cool, I’ll push a patch today. If anyone has strong feelings on “agent loop” vs “agent workflow,” reply here.

Monica Patel: vote: “agent loop” (more specific) + “workflow” as the overall app.

Allison Grant: +1 agent loop.

Elliot Price: same. locking in: “workflow” (overall), “agent loop” (pattern), “tool call” (operation), “RAG pipeline” (retrieval + context).

Nikhil Sharma: :white_check_mark:
